findings.what: premiumSubscriptionWithCompletion: reads a premium expiry that TDLib never sends: `long long expires = [TGPremiumNumber(state[@"expiration_date"]) longLongValue]; if (!expires) expires = [TGPremiumNumber(text[@"expiration_date"]) longLongValue];`
findings.failure: td_api.tl:8166 defines `premiumState state:formattedText payment_options:vector<premiumStatePaymentOption> animations:... business_animations:...`. There is no `expiration_date` on premiumState and none on its `state` (a formattedText, fields `text`/`entities`). Both lookups always miss, `expires` is always 0, so the `expires > 0` branch at line 219 is unreachable and `expiresText` is always the literal "Active". TGPremiumViewController.m:143-146 shows `expiresText` as the subscription subtitle, so a subscriber's Premium screen can never display the renewal date. The identical dead lookup exists a second time in TGClient.m:1481 (`state[@"state"][@"expiration_date"] ?: state[@"expiration_date"]`).
findings.fix: TDLib exposes no premium expiry on premiumState. Delete lines 213-217 and the `@"expires"` output key, and set expiresText from `active` alone ("Active"), or obtain the date elsewhere (e.g. cache `subscription_until_date` from the messagePaymentSuccessful service message in chat 777000) before claiming to show one. Apply the same removal to TGClient.m:1481 so the two copies do not drift again.

findings.what: `@"queryId" : TGBNumber(result[@"inline_query_id"])` treats an int64 td_api field as an NSNumber.
findings.failure: tdlib/td/td/tl/tl_json.h:29-31 serializes every td_api `int64` through `JsonInt64`, which writes `jv << JsonString(...)` - i.e. int64 fields arrive as JSON *strings*, unlike int53 (chat/user/message ids) which arrive as numbers. td_api.tl:7614 declares `inlineQueryResults inline_query_id:int64 ...`, so `result[@"inline_query_id"]` is an NSString, `TGBNumber` fails its isKindOfClass check and returns @0. The dictionary handed to the UI carries queryId 0, and -sendInlineResult:queryId:toChat:replyTo:hideVia: (line 587, `@"query_id" : queryId ?: @0`) then sends `query_id: 0`, so every attempt to send an inline-bot result fails with a TDLib "Wrong query_id" error and nothing is sent.
findings.fix: At line 578 use the string form: `@"queryId" : TGBString(result[@"inline_query_id"])`, and in -sendInlineResult:... pass that string straight through as `@"query_id"` (TDLib's from_json for int64 accepts String as well as Number, tl_json.h:91-101). Change the `queryId:(NSNumber *)` parameter in TGClient+Bots.h to `(NSString *)` to match.

findings.what: `@"id" : TGPremiumNumber(giveaway[@"id"])` in the prepaid-giveaway loop of -chatBoostStatusForChat:completion:.
findings.failure: td_api.tl:6828 declares `prepaidGiveaway id:int64 winner_count:int32 prize:GiveawayPrize boost_count:int32 payment_date:int32`, and int64 is serialized as a JSON string (tl_json.h:29). `TGPremiumNumber` therefore returns @0 for every prepaid giveaway. A caller that feeds that `id` into -launchPrepaidGiveaway:inChat:... (line 625) sends `giveaway_id: 0`, and TDLib rejects the launch with "Giveaway not found" - the prepaid giveaway can never be started from this client.
findings.fix: At line 697 emit the raw string: `@"id" : TGPremiumString(giveaway[@"id"])`, and change -launchPrepaidGiveaway: to take an NSString giveawayId and put it into the request unchanged (TDLib accepts String for int64). Same treatment for any other int64 field read through TGPremiumNumber.

findings.what: -instantViewForUrl:completion: can invoke its completion twice: `if (blocks.count && completion) completion(cached);` at line 876-877, then `completion(fresh)` at line 886 when the cached copy was not full.
findings.failure: A cached-but-partial instant view (blocks present, `is_full` false - the normal case for a first local hit) fires the completion once with the cached page and a second time with the network page. The only caller, TGInstantViewController (TGChatViewController.m:356), responds by calling -adoptBlocks: each time, which spawns a second global-queue layout pass over every block while the first is still running and then reassigns `_blocks`/`_heights` and reloads the table. On a single-core A5 the two passes contend, and because each pass publishes `_blocks` and `_heights` from its own async block, the table can be reloaded with the heights of one page and the blocks of the other (rows drawn at the wrong height, content clipped). Callers written against the header, which documents a single callback, have no way to know a second one is coming.
findings.fix: Either make the method single-shot - drop the early `completion(cached)` at 876-877 and always deliver the result of the onlyLocal:NO pass, falling back to `cached` when `fresh` is nil - or rename it to a two-phase API (e.g. -instantViewForUrl:progress:completion:) and update TGInstantViewController to cancel/ignore a stale -adoptBlocks: pass by tagging each pass with a generation counter.

findings.what: The premium gift-code and gift-premium API is implemented twice, in two categories on TGClient, with different result shapes: -checkPremiumGiftCode:completion: (Payments.m:1354) vs -checkGiftCode:completion: (Premium.m:447); -applyPremiumGiftCode:completion: (Payments.m:1379) vs -applyGiftCode:completion: (Premium.m:484); -giftPremiumWithStarsToUser:starCount:months:text:completion: (Payments.m:1385) vs -giftPremiumToUser:months:stars:message:completion: (Premium.m:525).
findings.failure: The two check-code flatteners disagree about the same TDLib object: Premium emits keys `months`/`days`/`used`/`creatorIsChat`, Payments emits `monthCount`/`dayCount`/`useDate` and no `used` flag, and Payments' `creatorId` (line 1366, `creator[@"user_id"] ?: creator[@"chat_id"]`) silently mixes user ids and chat ids into one key with no discriminator, so a giveaway created by a channel resolves as a user id. Only the Premium variants are reachable (TGPremiumViewController.m:607 -> -redeemGiftCode:); the Payments trio is never called from any screen. Anyone who wires a new screen to the Payments version gets a dictionary the existing gift-code UI cannot read.
findings.fix: Delete -checkPremiumGiftCode:completion:, -applyPremiumGiftCode:completion: and -giftPremiumWithStarsToUser:starCount:months:text:completion: from TGClient+Payments.m/.h (lines 1354-1400) and keep the TGClient+Premium.m versions as the single entry point.

findings.what: getStarTransactions is wrapped twice with incompatible output: -starTransactionsWithOffset:limit:completion: (Premium.m:1166, keys `refund`/`type`/`title`, returns a dictionary with `balance`) and -starTransactionsWithDirection:offset:limit:completion: (Payments.m:316 + -tg_flattenTransaction: at 271, keys `isRefund`/`userId`/`chatId`/`photoFileId`, returns array+offset).
findings.failure: Only the Premium wrapper is used (TGStarsViewController.m:264), and it never writes the module-static balance cache `TGPayCachedStarBalance` (Payments.m:92) that the same screen reads through -cachedStarBalance at TGStarsViewController.m:262. Paging the star history therefore never warms the cache, so every fresh entry into the Stars screen starts with `self.balance = 0` and `balanceKnown = NO` until a full transaction request completes - the balance row flickers from unknown to a value on every push, even though the value was already fetched a second earlier.
findings.fix: Keep one implementation. Simplest: in TGClient+Premium.m:1203-1205, after computing `balance`, also publish it - move the cache into TGClient+Private.h (or expose a `-setCachedStarBalance:`) and set it there; then delete -starTransactionsWithDirection:offset:limit:completion: and -tg_flattenTransaction: from Payments.m unless a caller for the direction filter is added.

findings.what: The entire TGClient (Bots) category - 734 lines, keyboards, callback buttons, inline queries, bot info, write-access - is unreachable.
findings.failure: No file outside TGClient+Bots.m imports TGClient+Bots.h, and no selector it defines (-inlineKeyboardRowsForMessage:, -replyKeyboardForMessage:, -pressCallbackButton:inChat:message:completion:, -inlineQueryToBot:..., -sendInlineResult:..., -botInfoForUser:..., -shareUsersWithBot..., -viaBotForMessage:..., -botServiceTextForMessage:) appears in any other .m. `reply_markup` is not read anywhere in the UI layer. -getCallbackQueryAnswer is additionally implemented a second time as -pressInlineButtonWithData:onMessage:inChat:completion: (TGClient+Messages.m:983), which is also uncalled. The cost is not only ~734 dead lines: the category is compiled and its +load-time method list is attached to TGClient at every launch, and the bugs inside it (see the inline_query_id finding) are invisible because nothing exercises them.
findings.fix: Decide the owner before wiring any bot UI: keep TGClient+Bots.m as the single bot layer and delete -pressInlineButtonWithData:onMessage:inChat:completion: from TGClient+Messages.m:983-1009 plus its header declaration, or drop TGClient+Bots.{h,m} from the Makefile source list entirely. Do not leave both.

findings.what: Large unreferenced blocks in Payments and WebLinks: the whole payment-form/receipt path (Payments.m:361-691: -tg_paymentFormForInvoice:, -paymentFormForMessage:inChat:, -paymentFormForInvoiceName:, -tg_sendPaymentForm:..., -payStarsPaymentForm:, -unlockPaidMediaInMessage:..., -validateOrderInfo:..., -payCardPaymentForm:..., -paymentReceiptForMessage:..., -clearSavedPaymentInfoWithCompletion:), the gift catalogue/collections/resale path (Payments.m:695-1233), and in WebLinks +flattenedLinkPreview:, +tappableEntitiesIn:, +linkPreviewOptionsDisabled:..., -linkForInternalType:isHttp:completion:, -publicLinkForUsername:, -publicLinkForStickerSetName:, -loginUrlInfoForButton:..., -loginUrlForButton:..., -deepLinkInfoForUrl:..., -applicationDownloadLinkWithCompletion:.
findings.failure: Verified by grepping every selector across src/*.m: the only live Payments entry points are -starBalanceWithCompletion:, -paidReactionSendersInChat:completion:, -addPaidReactionToMessage:... (TGReactionPickerView.m), -receivedGiftsFor... and -cachedStarBalance (TGStarsViewController.m); the only live WebLinks entry points are -resolveLink:completion:, -externalLinkInfoForUrl:completion:, -externalLinkForUrl:allowWriteAccess:completion: (TGChatViewController.m), -recentlyVisitedTMeUrlsWithReferrer:completion: (TGSearchViewController.m) and -instantViewForUrl:completion:. Everything else is compiled binary weight and untested surface on a device with 40-60MB usable RAM.
findings.fix: Trim to the live set, or move the speculative payment/gift/link surface into a separate file excluded from the Makefile until a screen actually needs it.

findings.what: `NSString *senderName = senderId ? [self nameForUserId:[senderId longLongValue]] : nil;` where `senderId` came from `sender[@"user_id"] ?: sender[@"chat_id"]` (line 803).
findings.failure: receivedGift.sender_id is a MessageSender (td_api.tl:1787), so a gift sent by a channel yields messageSenderChat and `senderId` is a negative chat id. -nameForUserId: looks that id up in usersById (TGClient.m:2226), which only holds user ids, so it returns nil and `senderName` becomes "". Gifts received from channels display with a blank sender in the Stars screen, and the `senderId` key gives the consumer no way to tell a user id from a chat id.
findings.fix: Mirror what Premium.m:463-466 does: record `BOOL isChat = [TGPayString(sender[@"@type"]) isEqualToString:@"messageSenderChat"]`, put it in the output under `senderIsChat`, and resolve the name via `[self nameForUserId:...]` for users and `TGPayString([self.chatsById[senderId] objectForKey:@"title"])` for chats (the pattern already used at Payments.m:1340-1341).

findings.failure: td_api.tl:1356 declares `premiumPaymentOption ... payment_link:InternalLinkType`, and the variants TDLib actually returns here (internalLinkTypePremiumFeaturesPage:9450 `referrer:string`, internalLinkTypePremiumGiftPurchase:9459, internalLinkTypeUnknownDeepLink:9528 `link:string`) have no `url` field. The `link` key of every payment option is therefore always the empty string, so any purchase button wired to it would open nothing.
findings.fix: Store the raw link object instead of a fabricated url: `@"paymentLink" : link ?: @{}`, and resolve it with -linkForInternalType:isHttp:completion: (TGClient+WebLinks.m:471) when the option is tapped. If nothing will consume it, drop the key.
